text:
lena (support): heads-up: SolarFlare on Dedicated reported a sudden p99 jump on /v1/generate starting ~2026-11-03T01:18Z. Customer says throughput also dipped. They attached some traces. @mike can you take a look? :warning:

mike (runtime): on it. do we have a sample request id or span?

lena (support): request ids: sf-req-9a3f and sf-req-9a9c in the trace. they say this started after our push yesterday (~23:40 UTC). logs attached in the ticket.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-20261103-011 (SolarFlare Dedicated p99 increase). Pager duty notified.

mike (runtime): thanks. quick check: is this only Dedicated for SolarFlare or observed elsewhere?

lena (support): SolarFlare only called it out. No other customers reported so far.

sanjay (perf): I pulled the kernel metrics for the ded pool that serves them. starting at ~01:15 UTC there's a sustained rise in GPU kernel % stall and host memcpy stalls. Might be memory thrashing.

mike (runtime): interesting. can you paste the exact grafana panel query?

sanjay (perf): panel: `sum by(pod) (rate(gpu_kernel_stalls_total[1m]))` and `sum by(pod) (rate(host_memcpy_wait_seconds_total[1m]))`. here's a tiny clip: ```
// top excerpt
2026-11-03T01:12:00Z gpu_kernel_stalls_total{pod="ded-sf-3"} 240
2026-11-03T01:16:00Z gpu_kernel_stalls_total{pod="ded-sf-3"} 820
2026-11-03T01:18:30Z host_memcpy_wait_seconds_total{pod="ded-sf-3"} 0.38
```

elaine (oncall): I just restarted ded-sf-3 to see if it clears. will monitor.

mike (runtime): good. also can we run the synthetic workload from the customer profile to reproduce? I'll kick off a short benchmark against the same model version and sequence length distribution. cmd: `./perf/run_benchmark --target ded-sf-3 --model gptx-1.3b --seq 2048 --clients 8 --duration 300`

lena (support): solarflare confirmed they were on gptx-1.3b, max seq ~1500.

sanjay (perf): running a dry run now on a staging instance. initial results show p50 stable, p95 OK, but p99 has spikes when GC on host occurs. suspecting host-side memory reclaim kicking in due to buffer fragmentation.

mike (runtime): that matches the memcpy stalls. if host OOM/fragmentation is the cause, a hotfix is to increase the host pinned buffer pool or change allocation strategy. can we get `pmap` and `dmesg` from ded-sf-3?

elaine (oncall): attaching `dmesg` excerpt from the restart: ```
[01:18:20] node: task killed: oom_reaper invoked
[01:18:21] kernel: tcmalloc: failed to allocate 64MB
```

mike (runtime): OK that's a smoking gun. customer restart helped?

lena (support): customer reported latency improved after we restarted the pod, but they expect a recurring issue if underlying cause remains.

sanjay (perf): proposed next steps: 1) instrument allocator to report fragmentation counters, 2) backport a change to increase pinned buffer pool size for Dedicated pools, 3) roll a canary for SolarFlare and monitor p99 for 6 hours.

mike (runtime): agree. I'll prepare a small rollbackable deploy with `PINNED_BUF_MB=8192` env on a canary pod and add allocation metrics to exporter.

elaine (oncall): I'll schedule the canary for 02:30 UTC once traffic quiets for the customer. tagging @lena to coordinate customer window.

lena (support): I told the customer we're doing a short canary at 02:30 UTC, asked for permission to route a small % of traffic during the test. They said OK.

mike (runtime): action items: Mike -> build canary + metric patch (ETA 30m). Sanjay -> add fragmentation counters and verify on staging (ETA 20m). Elaine -> restart watch and rollback playbook (ready). Lena -> keep customer updated.

ops-bot: Update: INC-20261103-011 status=investigating assignee=mike timestamp=1799123610

sanjay (perf): staging fragmentation counters show the same pattern when we simulate their request mix. I have a short snippet to add to the exporter: `allocator.frag_ratio = bytes_wasted / total_allocated`. will open PR now.

mike (runtime): cool. once PR is up ping me for review, will queue the canary deploy. :thumbsup:

lena (support): thanks team. I'll post verification steps for the customer and ask them to report any recurrences.

elaine (oncall): will keep watch on alerts. thumbs up. :white_check_mark:

mike (runtime): FYI if canary looks good we'll promote change to the whole dedicated pool during low-traffic window tomorrow. rolling upgrade with 5% batch size.

lena (support): noted. closing loop with customer that we have plan.

mike (runtime): closing notes: likely root cause = host memory fragmentation causing memcpy stalls -> p99 spikes. mitigation = increase pinned buffer pool + better fragmentation telemetry. will follow up in postmortem once resolved.

lena (support): thanks everyone. I'll update INC-20261103-011 with links to PR and canary results after deployment.
